column1: # .github/secret-reveal-allow.tsv — every place a secret.Value's bytes leave
# api/cmd/secretlint reports every selection of secret.Value.Reveal (SL01)
# and fails on one this file does not name. A row is a reviewed site: the
# reason says why the bytes must leave there. The gate also fails on a row
# that matches no site, so a row cannot outlive its code.
# SL02 (unsafe or reflect access to a type that holds a secret.Value) has no
# allowlist: there is no row that admits one.
# A row is keyed on path + enclosing symbol, never on a line number — the
# Checked by: go run ./api/cmd/secretlint <one ./module/... per go.work module>

column3: reason
Checks the key's length and that it is not all zeroes, and copies it into the session's own payload (secret.New), so the handler's Destroy cannot reach the session.
Copies the session's key into the stream grant's own payload under the lock, so a session closing mid-stream cannot zero the bytes an unseal is reading.
Derives the public key from the private key to prove it opens the claimed target; the X25519 derivation takes bytes.
Unseals the identity archive far enough to read the trusted manifest; Unseal takes the key as bytes.
Unseals one member into the restore stream; Unseal takes the key as bytes. The grant's copy is destroyed when the handler returns.

The compose into AppDeployCmd, and each resolved ${secret:} value into its typed SecretEnv map beside it (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#776), for the bus command to the target agent (ADR-0006 D11a); the only node-bound path that may carry a resolved secret (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The per-app leaf key into AppLeafCmd, the bus command to the app's node, immediately before marshalling (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
A private key into its owner-only file through atrest: the slot it is read back from (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The BMC credential into the configure bus command at dispatch, never the job spec (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The BMC credential into the selection fingerprint, so that a rotation re-pushes. The fingerprint is a keyed MAC whose key no ledger reader holds (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#827).
The stored Turing Pi credential into the probe bus command to the host agent, when the operator left the password blank (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The restore transfer credential into BackupRestoreVolumeCmd, the command to the node restoring the member (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The PPPoE secret into the apply command and the keyed state fingerprint (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#827).
The MAC key into hmac.New; no bytes leave (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#827).
The node enrolment pre-auth key into MeshEnrollCmd, the bus command to the node being enrolled (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The user-device pre-auth key, returned once in the create response to the operator who minted it; it is never stored (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The console root crypt hash into ConsoleRootHashCmd, the command to each target node (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The archive key's two wrappings into StorageClaimCmd, so the disk's marker holds them (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The archive key's two wrappings into the claim job's staging row (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The archive key's two wrappings into the claimed target's row (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
Compares the claim's two wrappings with the disk marker's before adopting; no bytes leave (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
The upload credential into BackupTransferCmd, the transfer command to the node sealing the member (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825).
Sets the store token as the X-Vault-Token header, the one place the store reads it; never the URL, the body or a log (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#758).
Escapes each value byte by byte into the kv-v2 write body, a buffer sized once and zeroed when the transport closes it (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#758).
Refuses a value that is not valid UTF-8 or parses as an RFC 3339 time before any request; only a value shaped like a timestamp is copied to a string for time.Parse (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#758).
The mock's copy in and copy out: each value gets its own payload (secret.New), so neither side's Destroy reaches the other (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#758).
Escapes an app key's plaintext or ciphertext byte by byte into the Transit encrypt or decrypt body, a buffer the transport zeroes when it closes it (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#1084).
The mock's stand-in ciphertext: the key's id and the plaintext, copied into a buffer that is cleared once the new Value holds it (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#1084).
Reads the mock's stand-in ciphertext back to its key id and plaintext, copied into the returned Value and cleared (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#1084).

The seal key into its owner-only file through atrest: rotation/<id> when staged, and seal-key when settled. The one place the key's bytes leave; the caller destroys the Value (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#830).
The seal rotation's per-handshake client leaf key (PEM) into tls.X509KeyPair, then destroyed; the leaf is never written to disk (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#830).
Scans a value in place for a NUL byte (bytes.IndexByte) before any store write; no bytes are copied and none leave (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#779).

Test support (identitytest is imported only by tests). Writes the synthetic, per-run database password into the owner-only env file docker reads with --env-file, so it never appears in an argument or in docker's output; the buffer is cleared after the write.
Test support. Writes the synthetic, per-run database password into the owner-only keycloak.conf Keycloak reads, as #959's template does; the caller clears the bytes after the write.
Test support. Writes the synthetic, per-run user password into the owner-only realm file Keycloak imports, JSON-quoted; the caller clears the bytes after the write.
Test support. Puts the synthetic test user's password in the sign-in form's POST body, the one place a password sign-in must send it; it is never logged and never in an error.

Form-encodes a temporary client secret byte by byte into the token request's body, a buffer sized once and zeroed when the call returns; never the URL, a header or a log (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#978).
Sets the Admin API token as the Authorization: Bearer header, the one place the identity service reads it; never the URL, the body or a log (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#978).

Copies the temporary recovery secret into the one line the OS's recovery launcher reads on its standard input (stdin), so it never reaches an argument, an environment entry the api sets or a file; the copy is zeroed on return and the launcher hands it only to kc.sh bootstrap-admin's own environment (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#1131, register row E39).

A runtime secret's value into AppSecretReply on a successful read, and an app key's ciphertext or plaintext on a successful encrypt or decrypt (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#1084), the reply to the app's own call, published only on a reply subject under the calling node's own command lane, which that node alone may subscribe to (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#1081).
Hashes the console session cookie (busauth.HashToken takes a string); only the hash is stored or compared, never the cookie (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#989).
Writes the console session cookie to the browser that just signed in: the one place the cookie's bytes must leave the api (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#989).
Hands the ID token to go-oidc's verifier, which takes the compact JWT as a string; the token is never stored or logged (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#989).
Hands the back-channel logout token to go-oidc's VerifyLogout, which takes the compact JWT as a string; the token is never stored or logged (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#989).
Form-encodes the authorization code and its PKCE verifier byte by byte into the token request's body buffer, which roundLocation zeroes once the call returns (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#989).

Hashes the new password with SHA-1 for the breached-password range query; only the first 5 hex characters of the hash leave the process, and the hash is zeroed before Listed returns (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#1145).
Hashes the typed repair code (Hash: canonical form, then SHA-256) to compare it in constant time with the outstanding code's hash; the canonical copy is cleared (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#321).
Hashes a repair session's cookie: the session is kept, and matched, as its SHA-256 alone (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#321).
Writes the repair session's cookie into its one Set-Cookie header, HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict, the one place it reaches the browser (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#321).

Copies the administrator's temporary password into Held's own payload (secret.New) under the new job's id, so the sign-in's Destroy of its payload cannot reach the job's copy; never the spec, a log or an error (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#992).

Copies the repair session's temporary password into Held's own payload (secret.New) under the new job's id, so the request's Destroy of its copy cannot reach the job's; never the spec, a log or an error (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#321).

JSON-escapes the password (temporary for an administrator's reset, not temporary for a moved account's first password) byte by byte into the reset-password request body, the one place the identity service reads it; the identity client zeroes the body once the call returns (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#992, geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#1005).
Hands a reset client's access token to go-oidc's verifier, which takes the compact JWT as a string; the token is never stored or logged (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#992).

Reads the password in place to count its UTF-16 length, compare it case-insensitively with the name and email, and match its lowercased copy, cleared on return, against the deny list; no bytes leave (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#992).

Takes an account change's held value (a new email address or display name) as the text the one Admin API write needs; the value is destroyed when the step returns and the text is never logged, recorded or put in an error (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#994).

Checks an account change's value at the request (an email address parses back exactly; a name or label is 1 to 255 characters with no control character) before it is held; only a fixed cause leaves (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#994).
Copies a TextBody (a credential's userLabel) into the request body, the one place the identity service reads it; the client zeroes the body once the call returns (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#994).

A moved account's first email, held as a secret.Value, as the text the removed-name check, the in-use check, the policy check and the one email write take; it is never logged, recorded or put in an error (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#1005).

Copies the bridge's password and email into Held's own payloads (secret.New) under the new job's id, so the request's Destroy cannot reach the job's copies; never the spec, a log or an error (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#1005).
